:::{#exm-linear-approximation-vector}
#### A linear approximation of a function of two variables

Take $f(\vcoef) = 3 \coef{1} + 5 \coef{2}^2$ from @exm-vector-derivative,
whose [gradient](#def-vector-derivative) at $\vcoef = \tp{(1, 2)}$ is $\gradf{f}(\vcoef) = \tp{(3, 20)}$.
At that point,

$$
\ba
f(\vcoef)
&= 3 \cdot 1 + 5 \cdot 2^2
&& \text{(substitute } \coef{1} = 1 \text{ and } \coef{2} = 2 \text{)}
\\
&= 23,
&& \text{(} 3 + 20 = 23 \text{)}
\ea
$$

so the [linear approximation](#def-linear-approximation-vector) at $\vcoef$ is

$$
\hat{f}_{\vcoef}(\stepvec) = 23 + 3 \step_1 + 20 \step_2.
$$

For the step $\stepvec = \tp{(0.1, 0.1)}$, the approximation is

$$
\ba
\hat{f}_{\vcoef}(\stepvec)
&= 23 + 3 \cdot 0.1 + 20 \cdot 0.1
&& \text{(substitute } \step_1 = \step_2 = 0.1 \text{)}
\\
&= 25.3,
&& \text{(} 23 + 0.3 + 2 = 25.3 \text{)}
\ea
$$

and the value of $f$ at $\vcoef + \stepvec = \tp{(1.1, 2.1)}$ is

$$
\ba
f(\vcoef + \stepvec)
&= 3 \cdot 1.1 + 5 \cdot 2.1^2
&& \text{(substitute } \coef{1} = 1.1 \text{ and } \coef{2} = 2.1 \text{)}
\\
&= 25.35.
&& \text{(} 3.3 + 22.05 = 25.35 \text{)}
\ea
$$

The approximation misses by $0.05$, which is $5 \step_2^2$,
the second-order term of $f$ that the approximation leaves out.
That term is never negative and is zero only when $\step_2 = 0$,
so the [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph) of the approximation in @fig-linear-approximation-vector
is a plane that touches the graph of $f$ along the line $\coef{2} = 2$
and lies below it everywhere else.
